segments.text: Hello explorers! Today we are doing a cool experiment. Actually, a cold one.
[scene: a tray of ice cubes on a table] Here are some ice cubes. Ice is water that got so cold it froze solid.
Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius. That is really cold.
[scene: ice cube in a hand] When I hold the ice, it starts to drip. Why is that happening?
My hand is warm. The heat from my hand moves into the ice and the ice turns back into water.
That is called melting. Heat makes ice melt.
[scene: two ice cubes, one in sun, one in shade] Let's put one ice cube in the sunshine and one in the shade.
Which one do you think will melt first?
[scene: the sunny ice cube is a puddle] The one in the sun melted first! The sun warmed it up.
The one in the shade is still mostly ice, because it stayed cooler.
[scene: salt being sprinkled on ice] Now let's sprinkle some salt on the ice.
Salt makes ice melt even when it is cold. That is why trucks put salt on icy roads in winter.
[scene: a glass of lemonade with ice] Ice in your drink melts too. It keeps the drink cold while it melts.
So heat moves from warm things to cold things. The ice gets the heat and melts, and the drink gets colder.
[scene: a freezer door opening] If we put the water back in the freezer, it will turn into ice again. That is called freezing.
Melting and freezing are opposites. Heat melts, cold freezes.
[scene: a snowman in the sun] Have you seen a snowman melt on a sunny day? Now you know why!
The snow is frozen water. The sun gives it heat, and the snowman turns into a puddle.
[scene: an ice cream cone dripping] Ice cream melts too, so eat it fast on a hot day!
Here is a challenge: what could you do to make an ice cube melt slower?
You could wrap it in a towel, or keep it in the shade, or put it somewhere cold.
[scene: a blue cup and a red cup] Let's try it. The blue cup is wrapped in a towel, the red cup is not.
After ten minutes, the red cup ice is gone but the blue cup ice is still there. The towel kept the heat out.
So remember: heat makes ice melt, and keeping heat away keeps ice frozen.
Thanks for exploring with me. Stay curious, and stay cool!
Bye!
